# The home's plan preview shows the board narrower than the Gantt chart

## Context

The operator, on the home's plan preview (Gantt chart above, task board below, one store), 20 Nov 2026: "task board and gantt charts not having the same width looks ugly." In his frame the Gantt fills the preview while the board's four columns stop about a tenth of the width short.

## The Problem

The preview's point is one plan in two views. Two different right edges make the views look unrelated, and the empty strip under the Gantt's last days reads as a layout bug.

## The Architectural Reality

- The preview runs the source string in `apps/portal/view/home/parts/Planning.mjs` (`Portal.view.HomePlanning`): a vbox with the Gantt (`height: 366`) and a `Board` (`flex: 1`) bound to `stores.plan`, with four columns from `colors`.
- The board's columns keep their own width, so four of them span less than the preview, while the Gantt's timeline fills it.
- Open question for the builder: does `Neo.board.Container` offer columns that share the available width? If it does, the preview sets it. If it does not, that is an engine gap to file as a blocker instead of fixing it in the preview.
- Design authority: the operator, 20 Nov 2026, quoted under Context.

## The Fix

Give the board's columns the preview's width, so the board and the Gantt share both edges at every width the preview takes. Keep the source string short: it is the preview's "48 lines" claim.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] The board's right edge meets the Gantt's at 1440 × 900 and 1920 × 1080, and at 390 × 844 the board scrolls or stacks as it does today without leaving a strip.
- [ ] The preview's line count stays within its stated "48 Lines", or the sub-headline follows the new count.
- [ ] Before and after frames of the whole preview on the pull request.

## Out of Scope

- The Gantt's tree-column sort, which the operator reported in the same message; it is tracked separately.

### @neo-fable-mnemosyne - 2026-11-20T20:45:14Z

**Intake: accepted, with one sharpening from the rendered page.**

The premise holds at 1440 × 900: the last column ends 89 px before the Gantt chart does.

**What the measurement adds.** The Gantt chart in the preview is 881 px wide in every window (a 160 px task column and 20 days of 36 px). The preview's pane is 889 px at 1440 × 900, so there the chart fills it. From about 1500 px of window width it no longer does: at 1920 × 1080 the chart ends at 881 of 1,209 px. A board that takes "the preview's width" would then run 320 px past the chart, the same defect mirrored. So I read AC-1's "the Gantt's right edge" as the right edge of the **chart**, and the fix gives the board the chart's width.

**The open question.** `Neo.board.Container` offers no columns that share the width: `createColumnConfig` pins `flex: 'none'` and drops a column's own `flex`. Its one sizing surface, the token `--neo-board-column-width`, does carry it, because a percentage in the token resolves against the board's content box. So the preview's stylesheet sets the token and nothing overrides the board's columns; I did not file a blocker. Undone in one line if the family's owner wants the engine option first.

**Two engine gaps, recorded as defect-notes** (mailbox, `AGENT:*`): `c9837d47` — a timeline cannot fit its viewport, which is why the chart stops at 881 px; `146ca5f0` — board columns cannot share the board's width by a config. With the first one built, the preview can fill its pane at every width and drop the cap.

Numbers and frames are on the pull request.
